title: What should you do if wind moves your replaced ball on the putting green?
question: After Robert marks, lifts and replaces his ball on the putting green, a gust of wind moves his ball before he makes his stroke. What should Robert do according to the Rules of Golf?

choices.text: Play the ball from its new position.
Replace the ball on its original spot without penalty.
Replace the ball and add one penalty stroke.

explanation: Under Rule 9.3, if a player's ball on the putting green has been lifted and replaced and then moves due to natural forces (like wind), the ball must be replaced on its original spot without penalty.

juniorVersion.title: What should you do if the wind blows your ball after you put it back on the green?
juniorVersion.question: Robert picks up his ball to clean it on the putting green and puts it back. Before he hits it, the wind blows his ball to a new spot. What should Robert do now?

choices.text: Play the ball from where the wind moved it.
Put the ball back where it was before the wind moved it. No penalty.
Put the ball back where it was and add a penalty.

juniorVersion.explanation: If you already marked and put your ball back on the green, but wind moves it, you need to put the ball back where it was. You do not get a penalty.

vocabulary.simpleMeaning: The short, smooth grass around the hole where you use your putter.
To put a small marker down to show where your ball was before you pick it up.

juniorVersion.teachingTip: Show kids how to mark their ball and where to replace it if it moves before they putt.
likelyMisconceptions: Some kids might think they should always play the ball from where it rolls to, but on the green after replacing, it needs to go back.
